Daily News

Science

Most of our measures of a key cognitive process don't agree

Global · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 06 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

A study published in Nature found that three widely used measures of cognitive reappraisal—trait questionnaires, task-based ratings, and amygdala down-regulation—show almost no correlation with each other. Using 40 fMRI datasets, researchers determined that these methods do not measure the same underlying process, indicating that current tools fail to effectively capture the capacity for emotional regulation.

Why it matters

The findings challenge the validity of current methods used to assess emotional resilience, a core component of cognitive behavioral therapy, and call for a fundamental reassessment of how reappraisal capacity is measured and interpreted.

Seabirds racing home over the ocean can get jet-lagged

Global · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 06 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

A study in Science found that Manx shearwaters experience jet lag when flying across time zones, causing their internal clocks to desynchronize with local time. This desynchronization skews their sun-based compass, leading to measurable navigational deviations of up to 15 degrees during homing flights. The findings were derived from GPS data of 3,688 foraging trips by 1,045 birds, though the study notes it is not a controlled experiment and cannot confirm other jet lag symptoms.

Why it matters

The research provides insights into bio-inspired autonomous navigation systems and suggests that studying animals that routinely experience jet lag may offer strategies to mitigate jet lag effects in humans.

NZ · Major · Previously featured

Briefing produced 01 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Climate Action Tracker (CAT) described New Zealand's climate policy rollbacks as "staggering," stating current measures are inadequate to meet 2030 targets without purchasing the largest proportion of offshore carbon credits in the world. CAT noted that under current policies, New Zealand would be 27-33% above 1.5°C-compatible levels by 2030, citing the scrapping of agricultural emissions pricing and the reversal of the oil and gas exploration ban. Climate Change Minister Simon Watts countered that the government remains committed to the Paris Agreement and cited a 2.9% decrease in annual emissions.

Why it matters

CAT warned that New Zealand's reliance on international carbon credits contradicts Paris Agreement guidelines, which require domestic policies to be on track before using such offsets, and noted no guarantee of sufficient high-quality credit availability.

Daily News

AI · Politics

Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.

United States · Notable · Catch up

Briefing produced 01 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

A study by Convovo found that when forced to choose candidates in nearly 500 US midterm races, SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 recommended Republicans in 92% of cases, while OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol picked Democrats in 97%. The models agreed less than 10% of the time, with Grok citing conservative sources and GPT relying on Wikipedia and AP. Testing with internet search disabled showed GPT’s bias persisted in its weights, while Grok’s Republican preference disappeared, suggesting its bias stems from search patterns and sources.

Why it matters

The findings highlight that AI models may exhibit political bias through search patterns and hidden instructions, potentially influencing users who rely on chatbots for election information despite consumer apps refusing to make direct recommendations.

Neural recordings from 248 neurons in the crows' NCL showed evidence accumulation similar to primate neocortex activity, despite the birds' distinct brain architecture. Why it matters

The findings demonstrate that evolution has independently converged on similar decision-making mechanisms in birds and mammals, offering insights into how different brain architectures process visual information efficiently.

Two Foodstuffs North Island supermarkets, Pak'nSave Silverdale and Pak'nSave Mill Street, were fined a combined $580,500 in Auckland District Court for repeated pricing errors that misled customers. The stores pleaded guilty to breaching the Fair Trading Act, with Silverdale fined $234,000 for 10 charges and Mill Street fined $346,500 for eight charges.

Why it matters

Commerce Commission deputy chair Anne Callinan stated the case highlights the necessity of a government review of the Fair Trading Act, which proposes increasing maximum fines from $600,000 to $5 million per breach to improve deterrence.

They warned against founders inflating annualized run rate (ARR) by counting short-term pilot customers as recurring revenue. Vohra advised tracking 'delighted ARR' to measure customer stickiness, while VCs emphasized that product-market fit must be continuously re-earned through innovation and honest revenue assessment.

Why it matters

The discussion highlights that inflated revenue metrics and low customer retention are critical red flags for investors, suggesting that sustainable growth requires distinguishing between pilot-based run rates and true recurring revenue.

The US Department of Justice launched Operation Ghostbusters to investigate a $200m student aid fraud scheme. Kenyan national Francis Mogambi was indicted in October 2026 for allegedly enrolling fictitious students and diverting aid to associates in Kenya. Investigators identified 830,840 potentially fraudulent accounts associated with nearly $130m in aid, a figure representing potential rather than confirmed losses. US authorities also seized over $750,000 in cryptocurrency from a Kenyan-linked account, a seizure not connected to Mogambi's individual case.

Why it matters

Victims of the identity theft face unexpected student loan debts and credit damage, while the scheme represents a significant drain on federal funds intended for student support.

Ford reports mixed third-quarter results, says 2027 earnings will be in line with this year

Global · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 30 Oct 2026, 9:21 PM NZDT

Ford reported mixed third-quarter results, beating earnings expectations but missing revenue estimates, with adjusted free cash flow of $4.7 billion. The company narrowed its 2026 adjusted EBIT guidance to $10.5–$11 billion and expects 2027 earnings to be roughly in line with 2026, citing offsetting factors like a $1.3 billion tariff refund and rising commodity costs.

Why it matters

Ford CEO Jim Farley described 2027 as a "foundational year" toward an 8% adjusted EBIT margin target by 2029, a goal analysts were previously mixed about achieving.

America's largest budget airline reports 71% jump in airfare

United States · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 30 Oct 2026, 9:21 PM NZDT

Frontier Airlines reported a 71% increase in third-quarter airfare revenue to $67.82 per passenger, driven by an 82% surge in fuel costs. Despite a net loss of $104 million, the carrier recorded an adjusted profit of $40 million and saw passenger numbers rise 18% to 9.8 million.

Why it matters

Frontier, the largest US budget airline, is passing record fuel costs to consumers while maintaining strong demand, illustrating how high energy prices are eroding carrier profits despite robust booking volumes.

Global · Useful · New

Briefing produced 30 Oct 2026, 9:21 PM NZDT

Starbucks reported mixed fiscal Q4 2026 results, with net revenue falling 4% to $9.14 billion due to its China joint venture transition, while U.S. same-store sales grew 7.7%, beating estimates. International sales underperformed expectations, but the company projects fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS of $3.15–$3.25, exceeding Wall Street forecasts, and anticipates a 1% revenue decline.

Why it matters

The company is ahead of schedule to meet fiscal 2028 targets, indicating its U.S. turnaround strategy is gaining momentum despite international challenges.

Cadillac Escalade IQ review: Huge battery, huge range, huge SUV

Global · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 30 Oct 2026, 9:21 PM NZDT

Ars Technica reviewed the Cadillac Escalade IQ, a heavy electric SUV with a 200+ kWh battery and a claimed 460-mile EPA range. The vehicle features 680 hp standard, air suspension, and a 55-inch display, weighing 9,046 lb. While it achieves 2.1 miles/kWh efficiency, equivalent to over 70 mpg, it lacks a published 10–80% fast-charge time.

Why it matters

The review highlights the Escalade IQ as a viable alternative to gas-powered models, offering significantly higher efficiency (over 70 mpg equivalent vs. 16 mpg for the V8) and substantial range, despite its heavy weight and premium price.
